sentences.text: Junichi Hanzawa, born January 19, 1965 in Saitama, graduated from the University of Tokyo's Faculty of Economics in 1988 and joined Mitsubishi Bank, now MUFG Bank, that same year.

sentences.text: He is a Japanese businessperson educated at the Faculty of Economics, University of Tokyo, who graduated in 1988 and joined the Mitsubishi Bank (now MUFG Bank) in the same year.

He became President and CEO of MUFG Bank and Deputy Chairman of MUFG in 2021, joined the MUFG board in 2022, and in April 2026 became Member of the Board of Directors and President and Group CEO (Representative Corporate Executive) of MUFG, while remaining a director of MUFG Bank.
His appointment, announced in December 2025, saw him succeed Hironori Kamezawa, who moved to the role of group chairman, effective April 1.

sentences.quote: Hanzawa, 60, who is currently the head of the main banking unit, will succeed Hironori Kamezawa on April 1, MUFG said in a statement on Tuesday. Kamezawa, 64, who has been CEO since 2020, will become chairman.
sentences.text: On December 16, 2025, MUFG announced a leadership overhaul effective April 1, 2026: MUFG Bank head Junichi Hanzawa, 60, succeeded Hironori Kamezawa, 64, as group CEO, with Kamezawa, CEO since 2020, becoming chairman.

Masakazu Osawa, 57, then a senior managing executive officer, took over as president of MUFG Bank, while Hiroyuki Seki, 57, became president of Mitsubishi UFJ Securities Holdings and of Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities; Seki left his post as board member and deputy president of the bank.
In July 2026 Hanzawa said he wants to achieve the goal set 20 years ago of ranking among the world's top five banks, targeting ROE in the mid-10 percent range.

Execution of the FY2024-FY2026 medium-term plan has run ahead of expectations: the roughly 9 percent ROE goal was reached in FY2024, prompting an increase of the FY2026 target to about 12 percent, alongside a CET1 ratio target range of 9.5-10.5 percent.
